# Manuscript 08 Reproducibility

## Question

The attached file is the current section specifying reproducibility and
failure conditions. Review and rewrite this section only.

Return a short critique followed by compilable replacement LaTeX.

Each row must state a concrete mathematical object and an exact criterion that
can be checked. Remove software-status language, vague evidence claims, and
anything stale. Keep analytic results distinct from fixed-kinematics numerical
comparisons. State the demonstrated scientific scope conservatively. Do not

## Pro response

Short critique

The table’s third column is framed as “required evidence,” but several entries are not exact criteria. “Correct distribution product,” “physical measure agree,” and “stated contour and branch” must be replaced by displayed identities or admissibility conditions. 

08_reproducibility

The causal row is incomplete. A shared real-emission denominator may vanish on soft or collinear boundaries; fixed sign alone does not justify removing i0. The complete term must also define a meromorphic integral in a nonempty convergence domain. 

08_reproducibility

The BMHV row checks only the absence of evanescent scalar products. It must also require exact reconstruction of the projected tensor integral, absence of integration momenta and unreduced physical tensor contractions from scalar coefficients, preservation of cut indices, and retention of the original D=4−2ϵ factors produced by the Dirac algebra. 

08_reproducibility

The IBP criterion “reinsertion reproduces every target” is ambiguous. The exact requirements are membership of each reduction relation in the module generated by the cut-aware IBP identities, transitive closure onto declared masters, idempotence of the reduction map, and positivity of every physical cut index. 

08_reproducibility

The finite-field row is too weak. Independent primes and unused-prime evaluations are comparisons, not a deterministic proof. Acceptance of an analytic coefficient requires a characteristic-zero rational identity, either directly or after clearing denominators. 

08_reproducibility

The master-evaluation row conflates analytic determination with numerical comparison. Differential-equation residuals, flatness, exact boundary data, normalization, contour, and branch define the analytic result. An AMFlow value is a separate fixed-point comparison and cannot repair a missing analytic condition. 

08_reproducibility

The final scope statement should say “one representative nontrivial NNLO post-IBP rational master coefficient,” not “one exact NNLO hard master coefficient.” The current wording also omits the solved four- and five-master families and could be read as stronger than the demonstrated calculation. 

08_reproducibility

\section{Reproducibility and exact stopping conditions}
\label{sec:reproducibility}

Every stage of the calculation is defined by a mathematical object and an
identity or admissibility condition that can be checked independently.  An
unresolved equality is not treated as true.  In particular, a timeout, a
failure to simplify an expression, or numerical agreement at selected
kinematic points cannot replace an exact identity.

Let
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb K:=\mathbb Q(D,\boldsymbol s)
 \label{eq:reproducibility-coefficient-field}
\end{equation}
be the rational coefficient field of an integral family, where
\(\boldsymbol s\) denotes its independent external invariants.  Let
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak R_{\rm IBP}
 \label{eq:ibp-relation-module}
\end{equation}
denote the \(\mathbb K\)-module generated by the cut-aware total-derivative
relations in Eq.~\eqref{eq:ibp-identity}.  Tables
\ref{tab:stage-criteria} and \ref{tab:analytic-stage-criteria} state the
conditions imposed on the successive objects.

  &
  Mathematical object
  &
  Exact acceptance criterion
  \\
  \midrule

  Leading-twist projection
  &
  Projected ordered interference
  \(\mathscr P_{\mathsf P}
  [\mathfrak M_i^F\mathfrak M_j^C]\)
  &
  For UU and LL,
  \[
   \mathscr P_{\mathsf P}
   [\mathfrak M_i^F\mathfrak M_j^C]
   =
   \mathscr F^{\mathsf P}
   \widehat{\mathcal C}_{ij}^{\mathsf P}.
  \]
  For TT, the corresponding tensor is decomposed exactly in the declared
  independent physical azimuthal tensors.  The difference between the two
  sides is zero, and the scalar coefficients contain no open Dirac, color, or
  Lorentz index and no PDF or FF outside the declared
  \(\mathscr F^{\mathsf P}\).
  \\

  Phase space and physical cuts
  &
  Pulled-back \(m\)-particle cut measure
  &
  With
  \(k_m=q-\sum_{r=1}^{m-1}k_r\), the original measure satisfies exactly
  \[
   \dd\Phi_m
   =
   \prod_{r=1}^{m-1}
   \left[
    \frac{\dd^Dk_r}{(2\pi)^D}
    2\pi\mathcal C_+^{(1)}(k_r^2;k_r)
   \right]
   2\pi\mathcal C_+^{(1)}(k_m^2;k_m).
  \]
  Every cut momentum is future directed, contains no virtual loop momentum,
  and retains its stated energy orientation.
  \\

  Causal admissibility
  &
  Denominator record
  \((\Delta_i,\tau_i,\chi_i,\xi_i)\)
  &
  An active forward denominator carries \(+i0\), an active conjugate
  denominator carries \(-i0\), and every cut has its declared \(\xi_i\).
  An active mixed forward--conjugate denominator is inadmissible.  An active
  shared-real denominator must be nonzero in the open physical domain; if it
  vanishes on a declared boundary stratum, the complete term must admit
  charts of the form
  \[
   \prod_a\rho_a^{A_a+B_a\eps}U(\boldsymbol\rho,\eps),
   \qquad
   U(\boldsymbol0,\eps)\neq0,
  \]
  with a common nonempty domain satisfying
  \(\operatorname{Re}(A_a+B_a\eps)>-1\) for every \(a\).
  \\

  Partial fractions and family completion
  &
  Fixed-cut decomposition into complete families
  &
  In the fixed-cut algebra,
  \[
   I_{\rm literal}
   -
   \sum_\alpha I_\alpha^{\rm independent}
   =0.
  \]
  Every retained term has
  \(\nu_{\alpha c}>0\) for every physical cut \(c\), and each completed
  denominator matrix obeys
  \[
   \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}A_\alpha
   =
   N_{\rm sp}.
  \]
  Cut identity, energy orientation, and measurement labels are unchanged.
  \\

  BMHV tensor and dimension recurrences
  &
  Scalar decomposition
  \(\mathcal A_D=\sum_\kappa C_\kappa I_\kappa^{(D)}\)
  &
  The displayed decomposition reconstructs the projected
  \(D\)-dimensional integral exactly.  Each
  \(C_\kappa\) is independent of every integration momentum and contains no
  \(\mu_{ij}\), no unreduced contraction with a physical spin vector, and no
  open tensor index.  Every physical cut index remains positive.  Explicit
  factors of \(D=4-2\eps\) generated by the original Dirac algebra are not
  replaced by \(D+2r\).
  \\

  Reuse of a powered family
  &
  Witness
  \((\rho,A,B,\pi)\) for
  \((\mathcal T,\boldsymbol\nu)
  \sim_{\rm pow}
  (\mathcal T',\boldsymbol\nu')\)
  &
  The witness satisfies all conditions of
  Appendix~\ref{app:topology-equivalence}, including
  \(\det A=\pm1\), exact denominator-slot permutation, preservation of the
  kinematic chamber, branches, causal classes, cuts, measurement labels, and
  index vector.  The resulting identity is
  \[
   I_{\mathcal T}^{(D)}
   \bigl(\boldsymbol\nu;\rho(\boldsymbol p')\bigr)
   =
   I_{\mathcal T'}^{(D)}
   \bigl(\pi_\ast\boldsymbol\nu;\boldsymbol p'\bigr).
  \]
  An explicit numerator insertion not encoded by family indices must obey its
  own pullback identity.
  \\

  IBP reduction
  &
  Exact reduction map
  \(\mathcal R:I_t\mapsto\sum_aR_{ta}M_a\)
  &
  For every requested target,
  \[
   I_t-\sum_aR_{ta}M_a\in\mathfrak R_{\rm IBP}.
  \]
  The closed map obeys
  \[
   \mathcal R^2(I_t)=\mathcal R(I_t),
   \qquad
   \mathcal R(M_a)=M_a.
  \]
  Every terminal integral is a declared master of the correct family arity,
  every physical cut index is positive, and no two rules assign different
  images to the same integral.
  \\

\subsection{Numerical comparisons}
\label{subsec:reproducibility-numerical-comparisons}

A numerical comparison is recorded separately from the analytic result.
For a physical point \(\boldsymbol x_\star\), let
\begin{equation}
 M_a^{\rm ana}(\boldsymbol x_\star,\eps)
 =
 \sum_{n=n_{\min}}^{N}
 m_{a,n}^{\rm ana}(\boldsymbol x_\star)\eps^n
 +
 O(\eps^{N+1})
 \label{eq:reproducibility-analytic-point-series}
\end{equation}
be the exact analytic Laurent series, and let
\begin{equation}
 m_{a,n}^{\rm num}(\boldsymbol x_\star)
 \label{eq:reproducibility-numerical-coefficient}
\end{equation}
be an independently computed numerical coefficient using the same family,
measure, propagator powers, cut orientations, causal prescriptions, and
external invariants.  A declared comparison tolerance
\(\tau_{a,n}>0\) is satisfied when
\begin{equation}
 \left|
  m_{a,n}^{\rm num}(\boldsymbol x_\star)
  -
  m_{a,n}^{\rm ana}(\boldsymbol x_\star)
 \right|
 \leq
 \tau_{a,n}.
 \label{eq:reproducibility-numerical-tolerance}
\end{equation}
Such agreement tests the normalization, causal boundary value, branch, and
analytic continuation at that point.  It neither determines the analytic
function nor supplies a missing boundary period.  The object entering the
hard function remains \(M_a^{\rm ana}\), not the numerical value.

\subsection{Scientific scope established here}
\label{subsec:reproducibility-scope}

The calculation presented in this work establishes:

\begin{enumerate}
 \item the exact six-master NLO real-emission cut system and its analytic
 solution;

 \item the two allowed NLO endpoint sectors
 \((1-w)^{-1-\eps}\) and \((1-w)^{-1-2\eps}\), together with their exact
 distributional expansion;

 \item exact independence of the demonstrated NLO UU and TT real-emission
 scalar coefficients from \(x_a,x_b,z_h\) and from auxiliary hadronic basis
 vectors after removal of the declared universal factors;

 \item the singular unpolarized NLO comparison for the coefficients of
 \(\mathcal D_1(w)\), \(\mathcal D_0(w)\), and \(\delta(1-w)\);

 \item the cut-aware reduction of the NNLO double-real contribution to a
 342-master Kira basis and its exact classification under the distinct
 powered-integral and positive-denominator relations;

 \item exact characteristic-zero reconstruction of one representative
 nontrivial NNLO post-IBP rational master coefficient;

 \item analytic solutions through \(\eps^2\) for the selected eight-, four-,
 and five-master NNLO cut families, together with independent fixed-point
 numerical comparisons.
\end{enumerate}

These results do not establish a complete polarized NLO hard function,
reconstruction of all NNLO rational master coefficients, analytic evaluation
of the full 342-master NNLO basis, or a complete NNLO hard function.
A stronger claim requires satisfaction of every applicable criterion in
Tables~\ref{tab:stage-criteria} and
\ref{tab:analytic-stage-criteria}.
